claims.text: The target phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys can form amorphous structures but have limited glass-forming ability.
The target alloys have limited thermal stability in the amorphous state.
Adding approximately 2–5 wt% boron will enhance glass-forming ability relative to an otherwise comparable alloy without boron.
Adding approximately 2–5 wt% boron will improve the thermal stability of the amorphous state relative to the unmodified baseline.
The proposed benefit should occur under rapid-solidification conditions similar to those used for the baseline alloy.
Homogeneous incorporation of boron without phase separation or excessive embrittlement is required for the proposed benefit.
Boron addition will improve short-to-medium-range atomic order.
Boron addition will enhance atomic-network connectivity by modifying local bonding environments.
Boron will disrupt local atomic clusters that favor crystallization.
Disruption of crystallization-favoring clusters will broaden the supercooled-liquid region.
Disruption of crystallization-favoring clusters will stabilize the amorphous structure against thermal fluctuations.
The boron-modified alloy will have a higher crystallization temperature than the unmodified baseline.
The improvement will occur only within an optimal low-concentration range of boron.
Boron concentrations above an unspecified threshold may cause phase separation.
Boron concentrations above an unspecified threshold may promote brittle intermetallic formation.
